name: National Domestic Violence Hotline
summary: 24/7 confidential support for survivors of domestic and intimate partner violence and their loved ones.

sections.title: About The National Domestic Violence Hotline
sections.text: The National Domestic Violence Hotline (also known as The Hotline) is a nonprofit organization that provides crisis intervention, safety planning, information, and referrals to victims and survivors of domestic violence, their friends, and families. Operating 24/7 since 1996, The Hotline has answered millions of calls and helped countless people take their first steps toward safety and healing.

sections.title: Who Should Reach Out
sections.text: The Hotline serves anyone experiencing domestic violence, dating abuse, or stalking, as well as friends, family members, and co-workers who want to help a loved one. You can reach out whether you're in immediate danger, planning to leave an abusive relationship, already left but need support, or just need someone to talk to about your situation. There is no wrong reason to call.

sections.title: How to Contact The Hotline
sections.text: Call 1-800-799-SAFE (7233) available 24/7, 365 days a year. Text START to 88788. Chat online at thehotline.org. TTY users can call 1-800-787-3224. Services are available in English and Spanish, with access to interpreters in over 200 languages. All contact is confidential, and advocates understand how to protect your safety and privacy.

sections.title: What to Expect When You Contact The Hotline
sections.text: When you reach out, a trained advocate will listen without judgment and help you explore your options. Advocates can help with safety planning, understanding the dynamics of abuse, exploring your options, finding local resources such as shelters and legal services, and emotional support. You don't have to make any decisions during the call—advocates are there to support you wherever you are in your journey.

sections.title: Safety Planning Resources
sections.text: The Hotline website offers safety planning resources including tips for staying safe while in a relationship, how to safely leave, digital safety and privacy protection, and information about protective orders. Advocates can help create a personalized safety plan that addresses your specific situation. If you're using a shared device, learn how to clear your browsing history to protect your privacy.
